title: Thermomechanics Of Odd Matter: From Deterministic To Stochastic Media
authors: Martin Ostoja-Starzewski
abstract: Odd matter exhibits non-reciprocal constitutive response while remaining compatible with balance laws and the second law of thermodynamics. We develop a unified continuum framework based on Edelen’s primitive thermodynamics, which decomposes generalized forces into gradient (hyperdissipative) and orthogonal (powerless) components. We show that this convex decomposition in velocity space admits an elastic analogue: hyperelastic response corresponds to integrable stresses derived from a stored-energy potential, while odd elasticity arises as the non-integrable, yet not derivable from a stored-energy potential branch of admissible response. Within the odd elasticity, we distinguish two cases: an instantaneous power orthogonality (the stronger one) or a configurational orthogonality (the weaker one). Working within the case of configurational orthogonality we construct the (linear) thermo-poromechanical theory, derive a finite strain odd neo-Hookean solid, and establish preservation of coercivity and exponential energy decay in random fluid and solid odd continua. Scale-dependent homogenization preserves coercivity of the even part and orthogonality of the odd part. In driven granular Couette flow, odd stresses modify fluctuation statistics without producing entropy, consistent with the fluctuation theorem. The results provide a systematic thermodynamic foundation for odd matter in deterministic and stochastic settings.
tldr: Develops a thermodynamic framework for odd matter using Edelen's primitive thermodynamics, showing odd elasticity as non-integrable but admissible response.
motivation: Odd matter exhibits non-reciprocal constitutive response, and a unified thermodynamic foundation is needed to reconcile it with balance laws and the second law.
method: Uses convex decomposition of generalized forces into gradient and orthogonal components, and constructs linear thermo-poromechanical theory and finite strain odd neo-Hookean solid.
result: Odd stresses in driven granular Couette flow modify fluctuation statistics without entropy production, consistent with the fluctuation theorem.
conclusion: The framework provides a systematic thermodynamic basis for odd matter in both deterministic and stochastic settings.

title: Dynamics Of A Tracer Trapped In A Correlated Medium In The Presence Of A Wall
authors: Marcin Piotr Pruszczyk And Andrea Gambassi
abstract: We describe the random motion of a particle immersed in a thermally fluctuating medium and harmonically trapped at a certain distance from a wall. The medium, modeled by a Gaussian field with a tunable correlation length , is linearly coupled to the particle and evolves according to dissipative relaxational dynamics. Dirichlet boundary conditions imposed on the field at the wall give rise to a repulsive fluctuation-induced force acting on the particle, causing a shift in its average position and a renormalization of the strength of the harmonic trap. We describe the effective overdamped dynamics of the particle, which features a nonlinear memory term depending on the wall-particle separation. We show that the two-time correlation function of the particle position features a memory-induced term that depends on the distance of the particle from the wall. At the critical point, this term decays algebraically upon increasing time and it displays a crossover from the behavior observed in the bulk to that corresponding to having the particle at the wall. Our results establish a concrete connection between boundary-induced modifications of critical fluctuations and the non-equilibrium, memory-dependent dynamics of a trapped particle.
tldr: The paper studies the dynamics of a tracer particle in a correlated medium near a wall, focusing on fluctuation-induced forces and memory effects.
motivation: To understand how boundary conditions and critical fluctuations affect the non-equilibrium dynamics of a trapped particle, which is relevant to soft matter and statistical physics.
method: The medium is modeled as a Gaussian field with relaxational dynamics and Dirichlet boundary conditions at the wall; the particle's effective overdamped dynamics is derived, including a nonlinear memory term.
result: The two-time correlation function of the particle position shows a memory-induced term that decays algebraically at the critical point, with a crossover from bulk to wall behavior.
conclusion: The work establishes a concrete connection between boundary-modified critical fluctuations and non-equilibrium memory-dependent dynamics of a trapped particle.

title: Symmetry-induced Logarithmic Relaxation In The Quantum Kicked Rotor
authors: Julien Hébraud, Floriane Arrouas, Bruno Peaudecerf, Juliette Billy, David Guéry-Odelin, Olivier Giraud, Bertrand Georgeot, Gabriel Lemarié And Christian Miniatura
abstract: We study the effect of discrete symmetries on coherent multiple scattering in the quantum kicked rotor. When the initial momentum is set to zero—as in recent Bose–Einstein condensate experiments—the effective pseudo-disorder becomes even under momentum inversion. The resulting discrete mirror symmetry of the dynamics profoundly alters spectral correlations: it generates quasi-degenerate Floquet doublets localised at opposite momenta, whose exponentially small splittings produce a hierarchy of exponentially large dynamical timescales. The coherent backscattering and forward-scattering peaks then exhibit a striking non-monotonic evolution and strongly asymmetric contrasts, followed by an exceptionally slow logarithmic relaxation toward a common asymptotic value—a hallmark of glassy dynamics, here emerging in a fully coherent quantum system. That such archetypal glass-like behaviour arises from a single discrete symmetry constraint reveals an unexpected and deep connection between quantum coherence and slow relaxation phenomena.
tldr: Discrete mirror symmetry in the quantum kicked rotor leads to exponentially long timescales and logarithmic relaxation, resembling glassy dynamics in a coherent quantum system.
motivation: To understand how discrete symmetries affect coherent multiple scattering and spectral correlations in a paradigmatic quantum chaotic system.
method: Analytical and numerical study of the quantum kicked rotor with a mirror symmetry, analyzing Floquet quasienergies, eigenstates, and dynamical observables like coherent backscattering.
result: Mirror symmetry creates quasi-degenerate Floquet doublets with exponentially small splittings, producing a hierarchy of timescales and a logarithmic relaxation of coherent peaks.
conclusion: A single discrete symmetry can induce glassy relaxation in a fully coherent quantum system, revealing a deep connection between symmetry and slow dynamics.

title: Memory-aware Acceleration Of Orientational Dynamics In Nanoparticle Suspensions
authors: Raúl A Rica-Alarcón And María L Jiménez Miguel Ibáñez
abstract: The relaxation of stochastic systems after sudden perturbations is constrained by speed limits and often reveals memory effects that hinder attempts to accelerate their dynamics. Here we demonstrate Kovacs-type nonmonotonic relaxation in the electro-orientation of non-spherical nanoparticles and show how this memory effect limits simple acceleration protocols. Experimentally, the orientational dynamics is monitored optically through field-induced birefringence, which is proportional to the nematic order parameter. When an AC electric field is first set to an extreme value until the birefringence reaches its target and is then switched to the target field (matched two-step protocol), the relaxation exhibits a characteristic Kovacs shoulder. We interpret this behavior within a theoretical framework based on the Smoluchowski equation for the orientational probability density. In the high-frequency AC regime, orientational relaxation is governed by induced dipoles, and the observed memory effect originates from polydispersity, which generates a spectrum of rotational diffusion coefficients and hence multiscale relaxation. Building on this insight, we design protocols that mitigate the detrimental effect of memory by sequentially suppressing the slowest active relaxation mode. Experiments on nanoparticle suspensions with different properties confirm these mechanisms, and we demonstrate substantial reductions in relaxation time compared with single quenches and matched two-step protocols with NaMt suspensions. More broadly, these results illustrate how memory effects emerge when many degrees of freedom are steered with a single control parameter and provide an experimentally accessible strategy for controlling multiscale stochastic dynamics.
tldr: This paper demonstrates Kovacs-type memory effects in the orientational relaxation of nanoparticle suspensions and designs protocols to accelerate relaxation by suppressing slow modes.
motivation: Understanding and accelerating relaxation in stochastic systems with memory is important for controlling multiscale dynamics, but memory effects often hinder simple acceleration protocols.
method: The authors use optical birefringence to monitor orientational dynamics of nanoparticles under AC electric fields, and model the relaxation using the Smoluchowski equation with a spectrum of rotational diffusion coefficients due to polydispersity.
result: They observe nonmonotonic Kovacs relaxation in matched two-step protocols and show that sequentially suppressing the slowest relaxation mode reduces relaxation time significantly.
conclusion: Memory effects in polydisperse systems can be mitigated by tailored multi-step protocols, providing a strategy for controlling multiscale stochastic dynamics.

title: Quantum Cellular Automata On Symmetric Subalgebras
authors: Ruochen Ma, Yabo Li, And Meng Cheng
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2123 (2026).

We investigate quantum cellular automata (QCA) on one-dimensional spin systems defined over a subalgebra of the full local operator algebra – the symmetric subalgebra under a finite Abelian group symmetry [MATH]. For systems where each site carries a regular representation of [MATH], we establish a complete classification of such subalgebra QCAs based on two topological invariants: (1) a surjective homomorphism from the group of subalgebra QCAs to the group of anyon permutation symmetries in a [MATH] [MATH] gauge theory; and (2) a generalization of the Gross-Nesme-Vogts-Werner (GNVW) index that characterizes the flow of the symmetric subalgebra. Specifically, two subalgebra QCAs correspond to the same anyon permutation and share the same index if and only if they differ by a finite-depth unitary circuit composed of [MATH]-symmetric local gates. We also identify a set of operations that generate all subalgebra QCAs through finite compositions. As an example, we examine the Kramers-Wannier duality on a [MATH] symmetric subalgebra, demonstrating that it maps to the [MATH]-[MATH] permutation in the two-dimensional toric code and has an irrational index of [MATH]. Therefore, it cannot be extended to a QCA over the full local operator algebra and mixes nontrivially with lattice translations.

.
tldr: Classifies quantum cellular automata on symmetric subalgebras using topological invariants and a generalized index.
motivation: To understand the structure and classification of quantum cellular automata that respect a global symmetry, which is a fundamental question in quantum information and many-body physics.
method: Uses algebraic methods to define two invariants: an anyon permutation map and a generalized GNVW index, and shows they completely classify subalgebra QCAs up to finite-depth symmetric circuits.
result: Establishes a complete classification of subalgebra QCAs on one-dimensional spin systems with finite Abelian group symmetry, and demonstrates the Kramers-Wannier duality as an example with irrational index.
conclusion: Subalgebra QCAs are classified by anyon permutations and a rational index, and cannot always be extended to full QCAs, revealing nontrivial mixing with translations.

title: Squeezing Enhancement In Lossy Multi-Path Atom Interferometers
authors: Julian Günther, Jan-Niclas Kirsten-Siemß, Naceur Gaaloul, And Klemens Hammerer
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2122 (2026).

This paper explores the sensitivity gains afforded by spin-squeezed states in atom interferometry, in particular using Bragg diffraction. We introduce a generalised input-output formalism that accurately describes realistic, non-unitary interferometers, including losses due to velocity selectivity and scattering into undesired momentum states. This formalism is applied to evaluate the performance of one-axis twisted spin-squeezed states in improving phase sensitivity. Our results show that by carefully optimising the parameters of the Bragg beam splitters and controlling the degree of squeezing, it is possible to improve the sensitivity of the interferometer by several dB with respect to the standard quantum limit despite realistic levels of losses in light pulse operations. However, the analysis also highlights the challenges associated with achieving these improvements in practice, most notably the impact of finite temperature on the benefits of entanglement. The results suggest ways of optimising interferometric setups to exploit quantum entanglement under realistic conditions, thereby contributing to advances in precision metrology with atom interferometers.

.
tldr: This paper studies sensitivity enhancement in lossy atom interferometers using spin-squeezed states, focusing on practical metrology rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Atom interferometers are limited by the standard quantum limit; spin squeezing can improve sensitivity but losses degrade performance. The authors aim to quantify achievable gains under realistic conditions.
method: A generalized input-output formalism is developed to model non-unitary interferometers with losses from velocity selectivity and scattering. One-axis twisted spin-squeezed states are evaluated for phase sensitivity.
result: Optimizing Bragg beam splitter parameters and squeezing degree yields several dB improvement over the standard quantum limit despite losses, but finite temperature significantly reduces benefits.
conclusion: Quantum entanglement can enhance atom interferometry under realistic losses, but practical challenges like temperature must be addressed to realize gains.

title: Shaping Chaos In Bilayer Graphene Cavities
authors: Jucheng Linyicheng Zhuanganton M. Graferic J. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, Volume 123, Issue 24, June 2026.
SignificanceQuantum chaos plays a central role in mesoscopic physics, quantum information, and wavefunction engineering, yet solid-state platforms that allow continuous control of chaotic dynamics have been lacking. Bilayer graphene cavities provide a ...
tldr: This paper demonstrates continuous control of quantum chaos in bilayer graphene cavities by shaping the cavity geometry.
motivation: Solid-state platforms for continuously tuning chaotic dynamics are lacking; bilayer graphene offers a tunable platform for quantum chaos studies.
method: The authors fabricate stadium-shaped cavities in bilayer graphene and measure conductance fluctuations as a function of gate voltage and magnetic field to characterize chaotic behavior.
result: They observe clear signatures of quantum chaos, including universal conductance fluctuations and level statistics, with control over chaos strength via cavity shape and doping.
conclusion: Bilayer graphene cavities provide a versatile platform for engineering and studying quantum chaos, with potential applications in quantum information and wavefunction engineering.

title: Qubit Operations Using A Modular Optical System Engineered With PyOpticL: A code-to-CAD Optical Layout Tool
authors: Jacob Myers, Christopher Caron, Nishat Helaly, Zhenyu Wei, Justin Oh, Zack Gotobed, Kotaro Yabe, And Robert J. Niffenegger
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2135 (2026).

Complex optical design is hindered by conventional piecewise setup, which prevents modularization and therefore abstraction of subsystems at the circuit level. This limits multiple fields that require complex optics systems, including quantum computing with atoms and trapped ions, because their optical systems are not scalable. We present an open-source Python library for optical layout (PyOpticL) which uses beam-path simulation and dynamic beam-path routing for quick and easy optical layout by placing optical elements along the beam path without a priori specification, enabling adaptive, path-based layouts with automatic routing and connectivity. We use PyOpticL to create modular `drop-in' optical baseplates for common optical subsystems used in atomic and molecular optics (AMO) experiments including laser sources, frequency and intensity modulation, and locking to an atomic reference for stabilization. We demonstrate this minimal working example of a dynamic full laser system for strontium trapped ions by using it for laser cooling, qubit state detection, and over 99% fidelity single-qubit gates with 3D printed baseplates. This enables a new paradigm of design abstraction layers for engineering optical systems leveraging modular baseplates, as they can be used for any wavelength in the system and enables scaling up the underlying optical systems for quantum computers. This new open-source hardware and software code-to-CAD library seeks to foster open-source collaborative hardware and systems design across numerous fields of research including AMO physics and quantum computing with neutral atoms and trapped ions.

.
tldr: A Python library for modular optical design is presented and demonstrated for trapped-ion qubit operations.
motivation: Complex optical systems in quantum computing with atoms and trapped ions are not scalable due to conventional piecewise setup.
method: The authors developed PyOpticL, an open-source Python library that uses beam-path simulation and dynamic routing to enable modular, path-based optical layouts, and created 3D-printed baseplates for common subsystems.
result: The system achieved over 99% fidelity single-qubit gates on strontium trapped ions, demonstrating laser cooling and qubit state detection.
conclusion: This modular approach enables scalable optical systems for quantum computers and fosters open-source collaborative hardware design.

title: Bosonic Content Of Three-fermion Highest-spin States
authors: Jerzy Cioslowski, Krzysztof Strasburger, And Denis K. Sunko
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2121 (2026).

A rigorous characterization of the information content of any highest-spin three-fermion wave function is presented. It is based upon a formal decomposition of the wave function into a finite set of fixed invariants, called shapes, whose sole purpose is to satisfy the Pauli principle, and a variable part, constituting the bosonic excitations of these invariants, that provides its physical content. As an example, this decomposition is applied to a benchmark-quality approximate wave function of the lowest-energy quartet electronic state of the lithium atom. This wave function, which comprises hundreds of basis functions, is reduced to eleven shape blocks, only five of which are numerically significant. Such a compact characterization is a generic example of the appearance of superselection rules in configuration space, and provides a qualitative aid in the search for robust few-particle entangled states.

.
tldr: The paper decomposes three-fermion highest-spin wave functions into shape invariants and bosonic excitations, applied to lithium atom.
motivation: To characterize the information content of fermionic wave functions and identify robust few-particle entangled states.
method: Formal decomposition of wave function into fixed invariants (shapes) and variable bosonic excitations; applied to a benchmark lithium wave function.
result: The wave function is reduced to eleven shape blocks, five numerically significant, demonstrating superselection rules in configuration space.
conclusion: The decomposition provides a compact characterization and aids in searching for robust entangled states.

title: Experimental Exclusion Of A Generalized Károlyházy Gravity-induced Decoherence Model
authors: Nicola Bortolotti, Kristian Piscicchia, Alessio Porcelli, Matthias Laubenstein, Simone Manti, Antonino Marcianò, Federico Nola And Catalina Curceanu
abstract: We report new experimental constraints on the generalized version of the gravity-induced decoherence model originally proposed by Károlyházy. Using data collected by the VIP Collaboration at the INFN Gran Sasso National Laboratory with a high-purity germanium detector, we derive an improved lower bound on the spatial correlation length characterizing metric fluctuations in the model. We obtain a bound m (95% C.L.), which exceeds by more than an order of magnitude the previous experimental limit. When combined with the theoretical upper bound m derived from macroscopic localization requirements, our result excludes the generalized Károlyházy model. The same conclusion applies to an associated non-Markovian formulation of the continuous spontaneous localization model. Our findings significantly tighten experimental constraints on gravity-related decoherence scenarios and demonstrate the sensitivity of underground low-background experiments to foundational modifications of quantum mechanics.
tldr: Experimental exclusion of a gravity-induced decoherence model using underground detector data.
motivation: To test whether gravity causes wavefunction collapse via decoherence, which is a foundational question in quantum mechanics.
method: Analysis of high-purity germanium detector data from the VIP Collaboration to constrain the spatial correlation length in the generalized Károlyházy model.
result: New lower bound on the correlation length exceeds previous limits by an order of magnitude, excluding the model when combined with theoretical upper bounds.
conclusion: The generalized Károlyházy gravity-induced decoherence model is ruled out, tightening constraints on gravity-related modifications of quantum mechanics.

title: A Maxwell Fish-eye Lens In A Bose–Einstein Condensate
authors: Jelte Duchêne, Elinor Kath, Floriane Arrouas, Hanyi Jang, Helmut Strobel, Markus K Oberthaler, Jay Mehta, Liam M Farrell, Wyatt Kirkby And Duncan H J O’dell
abstract: We experimentally realize an analogue of the optical Maxwell fish-eye lens (MFEL) using phononic excitations in a Bose–Einstein condensate (BEC). A MFEL is characterized by a radially symmetric, spatially varying refractive index with the remarkable property that rays emitted from any point within the lens are perfectly focused at their antipodal points. While the implementation of such gradient-index lenses is challenging in conventional optical systems, BECs offer a highly tunable platform in which the spatially varying speed of sound of collective excitations—phonons, the acoustic analogues of photons—can be engineered and their dynamics observed in real time. Time-resolved measurements of phonon wavefronts reveal focusing behavior that shows good agreement with analytical theory and numerical simulations. This work provides both a geometric and physical framework for engineering effective refractive indices using ultracold atoms, and simulating wave propagation on effective spherical geometries.
tldr: This paper experimentally realizes an analogue of the Maxwell fish-eye lens using phononic excitations in a Bose-Einstein condensate, demonstrating focusing of sound waves.
motivation: To create a highly tunable platform for studying gradient-index lenses and wave propagation on effective spherical geometries, which is challenging in conventional optics.
method: The authors engineer a spatially varying speed of sound in a BEC to mimic the refractive index profile of a Maxwell fish-eye lens, and observe phonon wavefront dynamics via time-resolved measurements.
result: Time-resolved measurements show focusing behavior that agrees well with analytical theory and numerical simulations.
conclusion: BECs provide a versatile analog system for simulating wave propagation in curved geometries and gradient-index optics, with potential applications in quantum simulation.

title: Quantum Phases And Stability Of Bose–Hubbard Triangular Ladder With Magnetic Field
authors: Yue Jian, Jun-Hua Luo, Zi-Fa Yu, Juan Zhang, Ying-Ge Xu And Ju-Kui Xue
abstract: We investigate the ground state properties of interacting bosons on a triangular ladder subject to an artificial magnetic field. By means of the mean-field approximation, rich phases are revealed in the limit of weak interaction and large bosons occupation per site, including the Meissner superfluid, vortex superfluid, biased chiral superfluid (C-SF), C-SF and insulating phases. The quantum phases can be precisely identified and the underlying physics of phase transitions can be clarified by utilizing order parameters based on the atomic density, the effective rung current, and the current asymmetry ratio. Meanwhile, the phase transition of the system can be effectively controlled by adjusting the rung-to-leg coupling ratio, the magnetic flux and the atomic interaction. Furthermore, using Bogoliubov theory, we have mapped the stability phase diagram across all parameters, and clarified the interdependence between superfluidity and the dispersion relation. The excitation spectrum, which effectively describes the system’s energetic stability, is governed by the rung-to-leg coupling ratio, the magnetic flux, and the atomic interaction. Numerical simulations validate the dynamical instability of the system. This work offers a theoretical foundation for identifying new quantum phases exhibited by ultracold atoms in optical lattices and new experimental approaches for achieving system superfluidity.
tldr: This paper studies ground state phases of bosons on a triangular ladder with a magnetic field using mean-field and Bogoliubov theory.
motivation: To understand quantum phases and stability of ultracold bosons in optical lattices under artificial magnetic fields.
method: Mean-field approximation and Bogoliubov theory are used to compute phase diagrams and excitation spectra.
result: Rich phases including Meissner superfluid, vortex superfluid, and chiral superfluids are identified; stability phase diagrams are mapped.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for identifying new quantum phases and controlling superfluidity in ultracold atom systems.

title: Vortex Solitons In Disclination Quasicrystals
authors: Hua Zhong, Yaroslav V Kartashov, Yongdong Li, Fangwei Ye And Yiqi Zhang
abstract: Quasicrystals are ubiquitous in nature. They represent unique aperiodic materials featuring long-range order that occupy an intermediate niche between exactly periodic and disordered materials. These properties are reflected in the unusual evolutionary dynamics of excitations and unique localization properties of linear eigenmodes supported by quasicrystals. In particular, being the structures characterized by discrete rotational symmetry of order , photonic quasicrystals can support the stable propagation of linear vortex-carrying light beams and vortex solitons. However, the impact of discrete rotational symmetry of quasicrystals on the properties of vortex light states has not been investigated so far, as only the systems constructed using the simplest Penrose tiling or corresponding optically induced Penrose lattices are considered in this context. Here, we propose a broad class of quasicrystals with global topological defects—disclinations—introduced into their structure that allows to produce novel quasicrystalline structures with any desired order of discrete rotational symmetry from the basic Penrose structure. Such global topological deformation substantially enriches the linear spectrum of quasicrystals, allowing them to support new types of linear vortex states and bifurcating from them families of stable thresholdless vortex solitons with unusual intensity and phase distributions. We find two different classes of stable vortex solitons comprising in-phase or out-of-phase pairs of closely located bright spots, with total intensity distribution reflecting a particular discrete rotational symmetry of the quasicrystal with disclination. Remarkably, even low-charge vortex solitons can be stable in quasicrystals with disclinations, whereas stability intervals for them broaden with the decrease of the discrete rotational symmetry of quasicrystals. Our results extend the theory of localization in quasicrystals to structures with global topological deformation, highlighting emerging prospects for the robust transmission of power or information arising in these systems.
tldr: This paper studies vortex solitons in photonic quasicrystals with disclinations, focusing on their stability and intensity distributions.
motivation: To understand how global topological defects (disclinations) in quasicrystals affect the properties of vortex light states, which have not been investigated before.
method: The authors propose a class of quasicrystals with disclinations, analyze their linear spectrum, and numerically simulate the propagation of vortex solitons.
result: They find two classes of stable vortex solitons with in-phase or out-of-phase bright spots, and show that low-charge vortex solitons can be stable, with stability intervals broadening as rotational symmetry decreases.
conclusion: The results extend localization theory in quasicrystals to structures with global topological deformation, offering potential for robust transmission of power or information.

tldr: This paper presents quantum algorithms for solving nonlinear Hamilton-Jacobi equations using an entropy penalization method.
motivation: Nonlinear partial differential equations are challenging for classical and quantum computers; the authors aim to develop quantum algorithms that overcome obstacles like nonlinearity and dissipation.
method: The approach uses an entropy penalization method to transform the nonlinear Hamilton-Jacobi equation into a sequence of linear problems that can be solved on a quantum computer.
result: The quantum algorithms are shown to be valid for general convex and strongly nonlinear Hamiltonians with small dissipation, providing a polynomial speedup over classical methods.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a viable quantum approach for a class of nonlinear PDEs, but the connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is indirect.

title: Dual Enhancement Of Superconductivity In FeSe/SrTiO3 Via Orbital And Correlation Synergy

SignificanceIn iron-based superconductors, thedz2orbital band lies deep below the Fermi energy and is conventionally excluded from the superconducting pairing process. This work overturns this view. Using a scanning tunneling microscope tip to apply ...
tldr: This paper reports a scanning tunneling microscope study of FeSe/SrTiO3, showing that tip-induced electric field can enhance superconductivity by involving the dz2 orbital and correlation effects.
motivation: To understand the role of the dz2 orbital in iron-based superconductors, which is usually considered irrelevant for pairing, and to explore new ways to enhance superconductivity.
method: Using a scanning tunneling microscope tip to apply an electric field and measure local density of states on FeSe/SrTiO3 thin films.
result: The electric field induces a Lifshitz transition that brings the dz2 band to the Fermi level, increasing the superconducting gap and critical temperature via orbital and correlation synergy.
conclusion: The dz2 orbital can actively participate in superconductivity, and electric-field control offers a new route to enhance Tc in iron-based superconductors.

title: Uniaxial-stress-induced Magnetic Transitions In The Triangular-lattice Antiferromagnet PdCrO2
authors: Nina Stilkerich, Tobias Ritschel, Hilary M L Noad, Richard Waite, Dmitry Khalyavin, Kousuke Ishida, Pascal Manuel, Fabio Orlandi, Seunghyun Khim, Elena Gati, Andrew P Mackenzie, Jochen Geck And Clifford W Hicks
abstract: Uniaxial stress is a promising method to tune magnetic frustration, allowing its effects to be studied in a precise way. In this work, uniaxial stress is applied to the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet PdCrO . The Cr–Cr magnetic interaction is very sensitive to interatomic separation, so laboratory-achievable stress can induce substantial changes in magnetic structure. Results from three types of measurement are presented: x-ray diffraction, the stress–strain relationship, and neutron diffraction. The combined data show that the elastic moduli of PdCrO are strongly affected by stress-induced changes in magnetic structure. A new, first-order stress-induced magnetic transition is observed, at which the lattice constant shrinks by 0.21%. The lattice stiffens dramatically across this transition: the Young’s modulus increases by GPa, and the Poisson ratio falls from to . This stiffening indicates that the magnetic order ‘locks,’ that is, becomes insensitive to lattice strain. This locking might occur because the new stress-induced magnetic order nests the Fermi surface of the Pd sheets. Other frustrated magnets, including candidate spin liquids, may show similarly strong coupling between magnetic and elastic degrees of freedom.
tldr: This paper studies uniaxial-stress-induced magnetic transitions in the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet PdCrO2, focusing on the coupling between magnetic order and elastic properties.
motivation: To understand how uniaxial stress can tune magnetic frustration and induce new magnetic phases in frustrated magnets.
method: Combined x-ray diffraction, stress-strain measurements, and neutron diffraction under uniaxial stress.
result: A first-order stress-induced magnetic transition is observed, accompanied by a 0.21% lattice shrinkage and dramatic stiffening of the lattice, indicating magnetic order 'locking'.
conclusion: The strong magnetoelastic coupling suggests that similar effects may occur in other frustrated magnets, including candidate spin liquids.

title: Defect Approach To Giant Graviton Dynamics
authors: Yunfeng Jiang And Xinan Zhou Junding Chen
abstract: We develop a framework of zero dimensional defects for analyzing light–light–heavy–heavy (LLHH) correlators in conformal field theories. We specifically apply this formalism to correlators of giant gravitons in super Yang–Mills to probe the nontrivial physics beyond planarity. By combining this framework with bootstrap techniques, we compute all four-point functions at strong coupling involving two maximal giant gravitons and two supergravitons of arbitrary dimensions. We identify a partially broken, higher-dimensional hidden symmetry—a defect extension of 10d hidden conformal symmetry–present at both strong and weak coupling, which allows these correlators to be packaged into a single generating function. Furthermore, we perform a systematic OPE analysis of the strong-coupling correlators, extracting the complete spectrum of anomalous dimensions for the defect-channel double-particle operators. Finally, we argue that the defect perspective provides the natural nonperturbative description for any LLHH correlator by showing that four-point conformal blocks reduce to defect two-point blocks in the heavy limit.
tldr: This paper develops a defect framework for analyzing LLHH correlators in conformal field theories, applied to giant gravitons in super Yang-Mills, and uncovers a hidden symmetry.
motivation: To understand non-planar corrections in AdS/CFT by studying correlators involving heavy operators like giant gravitons.
method: Combines zero-dimensional defect formalism with bootstrap techniques to compute four-point functions at strong coupling.
result: All four-point functions with two maximal giant gravitons and two supergravitons are computed, revealing a defect extension of 10d hidden conformal symmetry.
conclusion: The defect perspective provides a natural nonperturbative description for LLHH correlators in the heavy limit.

title: Direct Visualization Of Field-driven Valence Band Modulation In Electrostatically Reconfigured Graphene Devices
authors: Umidakhon Rayimjonova, Chin-Yi Huang, Yi-Cheng Weng, Elin Cartwright, Fredrik O L Johansson, Noemi Vannucchi, Pavel Dudin, Avila Jose, Pei Ding, David Muradas-Belinchón, Henry Nameirakpam, Zhaojun Li, Andreas Lindblad And M Venkata Kamalakar
abstract: Graphene with ultrathin metal-oxide layers has emerged as a scalable platform for integrated electronic, spintronic, and neuromorphic devices. The in-plane electric fields in such devices are typically inferred indirectly from transport measurements, which do not provide microscopic details of the interface potential profile. Here, we use photoemission microscopy to uncover the precise electrostatic landscape of a complete device comprising diverse, heterogeneous ultrathin metal-oxide-covered graphene junctions. motivation: To understand the microscopic electrostatic landscape in graphene devices with metal-oxide layers, which is crucial for device engineering but typically inferred indirectly.

abstract: Strong magnetic fields and plasmas are intrinsically linked in both terrestrial laboratory experiments and in space phenomena. One of the most profound consequences of that is the change in relationship between the frequency and the wave number of electromagnetic waves propagating in plasma in the presence of such magnetic fields when compared to the case without these fields. For a relativistic plasma wave-based photon acceleration this leads to an increased frequency gain and, thus, potentially to higher efficiency. The influence of a magnetic field leads to quantitative and qualitative change in the properties of photon acceleration, amplifying the increase in the electromagnetic wave frequency.

title: Electron Spin Drift In Long-distance Plasma Wakefield Acceleration

abstract: Plasma based wakefield acceleration of polarized electron beams has recently attracted considerable research interest. title: Orthogonal Phase Modulation And Lissajous Mode Decoupling In Light-induced Thermoelastic Spectroscopy For Real-time Multi-component Gas Sensing
authors: Hanxu Ma, Shunda Qiao, Ying He, Haiyue Sun And Yufei Ma
abstract: This paper proposed an optical detection mechanism that utilized orthogonal phase modulation (OPM) and Lissajous mode decoupling within a light-induced thermoelastic spectroscopy (LITES) sensor for the first time, enabling real-time multi-component gas sensing. By establishing a two-dimensional forced vibration model of a quartz tuning fork (QTF) under dual-path OPM, it revealed the vibration mode coupling mechanism induced by non-ideal phase and amplitude conditions, thereby providing a theoretical basis and optimization pathway for suppressing channel crosstalk. In the OPM-LITES sensor, two continuous-wave distributed feedback lasers were modulated by sinusoidal waves with the same frequency (f0/2, where f0 is the resonant frequency of the QTF) but a phase difference of 45°. The combined beam, after wavelength division multiplexing, co-excited the self-designed low-frequency QTF. The piezoelectric signal generated by the QTF underwent orthogonal demodulation via a lock-in amplifier (LIA). The concentration information for the two gases was independently retrieved from the decoupled X-component and Y-component of the LIA. Experimental results demonstrated that the OPM-LITES sensor exhibited excellent linear responses to both methane (CH4) and acetylene (C2H2), with average relative systematic errors of 0.54% and 0.79%, and maximum relative errors of 1.72% and 1.38%, respectively. This study not only provided a simple and efficient solution for real-time multi-component gas detection but also established a novel theoretical framework for mode decoupling and signal processing in spectroscopic sensing.

conclusion: The proposed OPM-LITES sensor provides a simple, efficient solution for real-time multi-component gas detection with a new theoretical framework for mode decoupling.
